Below is a detailed plan to convert the DNA WebGL code (from the dna-webgl.mdc instructions) into a React component following our coding standards. The new component will reside in the 3d area (e.g. in /src/features/3d) and will be implemented as a client component in Next.js. Here’s the step‐by‐step breakdown:

–––––––
1. Create a new file  
   • File: `/src/features/3d/DnaVisualization.tsx`  
   • Mark the file as a client component by adding `"use client"` at the top.  
   • Import React, useRef, and useEffect.

2. Define the JSX structure  
   • Render a `<canvas>` element. Use a React ref (e.g. `canvasRef`) for DOM access.  
   • Apply Tailwind CSS classes to the canvas to mimic the original CSS (e.g. fixed position, full-screen, background black).  
   • Render the scrolling content by including a `<div>` with a class for pages (use Tailwind’s scroll snapping utilities, for example, `snap-y snap-mandatory`).  
   • Within that div, create multiple `<section>` elements (one for each view: DNA, torus, none). Use data attributes (e.g. `data-model="dna"`) and Tailwind classes (e.g. `h-screen text-white snap-start` with appropriate padding).

3. Initialize WebGL in a useEffect  
   • After the component mounts, grab the canvas reference and set its dimensions to match `window.innerWidth` and `window.innerHeight`.  
   • Extract and define the shader code as constant strings (vertexShaderText and fragmentShaderText) in the component (instead of relying on `<script>` tags).  
   • Create the WebGL context from the canvas and compile the shaders, attach them to a program, bind the vertex buffer, and set attribute pointers.  
   • Define helper functions (e.g. `m4.perspective`, `m4.translation`, rotation functions, and `m4.multiply`) that mirror the provided math functions.

4. Handle animation and updates  
   • Define arrays for vertices, velocities, targetPositions (plus additional physics arrays like vertexMass).  
   • Write a function `computeTargetPositions` that updates target positions based on the current model (using the dataset from the `<section>` elements).  
   • Set up an animation loop using `requestAnimationFrame` to update the WebGL state. In the loop:  
  - Update a time variable (`t`), recalculate the transformation matrix (including dynamic adjustments based on scrollY), and update vertex positions through physics calculations.  
  - Clear the canvas and draw the new frame.  
   • If needed, include the stats code for performance monitoring (or refactor it into a separate helper).

5. Setup an intersection observer  
   • Attach an observer (inside useEffect) to the `<section>` elements within the pages container.  
   • On intersection, call `computeTargetPositions` with the current section’s data-model value to update the animation's target state.

6. Convert original CSS into Tailwind classes  
   • For the canvas, use classes such as: `fixed top-0 left-0 w-full h-screen z-[-1] bg-black`.  
   • For the pages container and sections, use:  
  - Container: `snap-y snap-mandatory`  
  - Sections: `h-screen text-white snap-start p-10` plus responsive padding adjustments (e.g. using Tailwind’s responsive classes).

7. Cleanup  
   • In the cleanup function of the useEffect, cancel the animation frame and disconnect the intersection observer to prevent memory leaks when the component unmounts.

–––––––
This plan outlines the conversion process while aligning with our Next.js, React, TypeScript, and TailwindCSS guidelines. Once implemented, the component will render a full-screen WebGL canvas behind scrolling sections that trigger different animations based on their data-model attributes.

+     gl.attachShader(program, fragmentShader)
+     gl.linkProgram(program)
+

+ 
+     // Initialize arrays

+     const velocitiesArr: number[] = []
+     const vertexMass: number[] = []
+ 
+     // Fill arrays with initial values
+     for (let j = 0; j &lt; VERTICECOUNT; j++) {
+       verticesArr.push(Math.random() * 10 - 5)
+       verticesArr.push(Math.random() * 10 - 5)
+       verticesArr.push(Math.random() * 10 - 5)
+       velocitiesArr.push(0.0)
+       velocitiesArr.push(0.0)
+       velocitiesArr.push(0.0)
+       vertexMass.push(Math.pow(Math.random(), 2) * 0.05 + 0.05)
+     }
+ 
+     const vertices = new Float32Array(verticesArr)

+ 
+     // Function to compute target positions based on model
+     const computeTargetPositions = (model = 'none') =&gt; {
+       if (model === 'dna') {
+         for (let j = 0; j &lt; VERTICECOUNT; j++) {
+           const a = j % 2 // split into left and right dna string
+           let f = j / VERTICECOUNT
+           if (j % 3 === 0) {
+             f = Math.round(f * 30) / 30
+           }
+ 
+           const errorScale = 0.2
+           const errorx = errorScale * Math.pow(Math.random() - 0.5, 3)
+           const errory = errorScale * Math.pow(Math.random() - 0.5, 3)
+           const errorz = errorScale * Math.pow(Math.random() - 0.5, 3)
+ 
+           let x = Math.sin(f * 4 * Math.PI + Math.PI * a) * 0.3
+           let z = Math.cos(f * 4 * Math.PI + Math.PI * a) * 0.3
+           const y = (f - 0.5) * 4 + errory
+ 
+           if (j % 3 === 0) {

+             x = x * r
+             z = z * r
+           }
+ 
+           targetPositions[j * 3 + 0] = x + errorx
+           targetPositions[j * 3 + 1] = y + errory
+           targetPositions[j * 3 + 2] = z + errorz

+       } else if (model === 'torus') {

+           const pointY = Math.sin(b) * torusStrengthRadius
+           const pointX = Math.sin(alpha) * pointR
+           const pointZ = Math.cos(alpha) * pointR
+ 
+           const errorScale = 0.2
+           const errorx = errorScale * Math.pow(Math.random() - 0.5, 3)
+           const errory = errorScale * Math.pow(Math.random() - 0.5, 3)
+           const errorz = errorScale * Math.pow(Math.random() - 0.5, 3)

+           targetPositions[i + 0] = pointX + errorx
+           targetPositions[i + 1] = pointZ + errorz
+           targetPositions[i + 2] = pointY + errory

+       }

+ 
+     computeTargetPositions('dna') // Initial computation
+

+     let t = 0
+     const mediumDensity = 0.1 // 0 = vacuum, 1 = maximum drag
+     const gravitationalForce = 1e-4
+ 
+     // Compute matrix for the view
+     const computeMatrix = () =&gt; {

+       const zNear = 1
+       const zFar = 200
+       let matrix = m4.perspective(Math.PI / 3, aspect, zNear, zFar)

+       return matrix

+       if (canvas.width !== window.innerWidth || canvas.height !== window.innerHeight) {

+         const mass = vertexMass[vertexIndex]

+ 
+     const observer = new IntersectionObserver(observerCallback, observerOptions)
+     const sections = document.querySelectorAll('.dna-section')
+     sections.forEach((section) =&gt; observer.observe(section))
+ 
+     // Start animation loop
+     let animationFrameId = requestAnimationFrame(render)
+ 
+     // Cleanup
+     return () =&gt; {
+       cancelAnimationFrame(animationFrameId)
+       observer.disconnect()
+ 
+       // Cleanup WebGL resources
+       if (program) {
+         gl.deleteProgram(program)
+       }
+       if (vertexShader) {
+         gl.deleteShader(vertexShader)
+       }
+       if (fragmentShader) {
+         gl.deleteShader(fragmentShader)
+       }
+       if (vertexBufferObject) {
+         gl.deleteBuffer(vertexBufferObject)
+       }
+     }
+   }, [])
+ 
+   return (
+     &lt;div className={&#96;relative w-full h-full ${className || ''}&#96;}&gt;
+       &lt;canvas ref={canvasRef} className='fixed top-0 left-0 w-full h-screen bg-black -z-10' /&gt;
+       &lt;div className='snap-y snap-mandatory'&gt;
+         &lt;section
+           data-model='dna'
+           className='dna-section h-screen text-white snap-start pt-[60vh] md:pt-[60vh] md:pr-10 md:pl-[60vw]'&gt;
+           &lt;div className='bg-black/60 p-5'&gt;
+             &lt;h2 className='text-2xl font-bold mb-3'&gt;DNA&lt;/h2&gt;
+             &lt;p className='text-sm md:text-base'&gt;
+               Desoxyribonukleinsäure, meist kurz als DNA bezeichnet, ist eine aus unterschiedlichen
+               Desoxyribonukleotiden aufgebaute Nukleinsäure. Sie trägt die Erbinformation bei allen
+               Lebewesen und vielen Viren (nicht RNA-Viren). Das langkettige Polynukleotid enthält in
+               Abschnitten von Genen besondere Abfolgen seiner Nukleotide. Diese DNA-Abschnitte
+               dienen als Matrizen für den Aufbau entsprechender Ribonukleinsäuren, wenn die
+               genetische Information in RNA-Stränge umgeschrieben wird (siehe Transkription). Im
+               Falle einer Boten-RNA (englisch messenger RNA, mRNA) stellt die Abfolge von
+               Nukleinbasen darüber hinaus die Bauanleitung für ein Protein dar.
+             &lt;/p&gt;
+           &lt;/div&gt;
+         &lt;/section&gt;
+         &lt;section
+           data-model='none'
+           className='dna-section h-screen text-white snap-start pt-[60vh] md:pt-[60vh] md:pr-10 md:pl-[60vw]'&gt;
+           &lt;div className='bg-black/60 p-5'&gt;
+             &lt;h2 className='text-2xl font-bold mb-3'&gt;Random Distribution&lt;/h2&gt;
+             &lt;p className='text-sm md:text-base'&gt;
+               This visualization shows particles in a random distribution pattern.
+             &lt;/p&gt;
+           &lt;/div&gt;
+         &lt;/section&gt;
+         &lt;section
+           data-model='torus'
+           className='dna-section h-screen text-white snap-start pt-[60vh] md:pt-[60vh] md:pr-10 md:pl-[60vw]'&gt;
+           &lt;div className='bg-black/60 p-5'&gt;
+             &lt;h2 className='text-2xl font-bold mb-3'&gt;Torus&lt;/h2&gt;
+             &lt;p className='text-sm md:text-base'&gt;
+               This visualization demonstrates particles arranged in a torus (donut) shape.
+             &lt;/p&gt;
+           &lt;/div&gt;
+         &lt;/section&gt;
+       &lt;/div&gt;
+     &lt;/div&gt;
+   )
+ }
+

The DNA visualization component has been successfully converted from vanilla JavaScript to a React component following our coding standards. Here's a summary of what we've accomplished:

1. Created a React client component `DnaVisualization.tsx` that uses WebGL to render DNA strands, torus, and random distributions
2. Fixed linter errors and TypeScript type issues
3. Made the component responsive with Tailwind CSS
4. Added scroll-based animations with IntersectionObserver
5. Created a simple page component `DnaPage.tsx` that uses the visualization
6. Set up proper exports with barrel files for easy importing

The component maintains all the original functionality:
- DNA helix visualization
- Torus shape visualization
- Random distribution visualization
- Physics-based particle movement
- Scroll snap navigation between sections
- Rotation and animation of the 3D elements

The implementation follows React and TypeScript best practices, and the styling is done with Tailwind CSS.
